correctness.rationale: The exact derivative factorization is verified algebraically. The explicit entire-series inequality gives strict decrease of the crucial function A for every x>0; the other function G strictly increases. This proves the global phase-minimum dichotomy. The full-rank two-by-two inverse equations and positivity inequalities establish necessity, sufficiency, and unique reconstruction; the excluded equality cases have a zero elastic parameter. The checker passed 800 random forward/inverse cases, 24 synthetic inverse observations, monotonicity checks, and 4 near-critical asymptotic cases. No infinite conclusion is inferred from the sampled tests.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary 2013 paper derives the combined forward sheet model and measures wave dispersion, but does not in the examined central theoretical and data sections provide the exact two-observable feasible interval, unique joint positive tension/bending inverse, or global one-minimum theorem. The 2011 and 2014 comparators address nonlinear/deep-water or pure-bending regimes. The 2021 application treats critical speeds and varying known elasticity rather than this exact joint inverse. Searches for alternate minimum-speed, stationarity, phase/group-speed, hydroelastic and rigidity/tension aliases did not identify an implication that subsumes the exact claim. Unreadable papers and implicit historical formulations remain documented priority risks.
residual_risks: Historical literature may express the exact inverse through phase/group-speed tangency or critical moving-load speeds without using inverse-theorem terminology.
Complete 2014 primary PDF was inaccessible; only indexed excerpts were examined, so its appendices/results were not ruled out.
Other older plate/water-wave and newer specialized sources were not exhaustively checked; originality is best-knowledge, not a uniqueness certificate over all publications.

value.rationale: The physically measurable phase-speed minimum is a natural forcing threshold. A two-parameter joint inverse from precisely two scalars with a necessary-and-sufficient open admissible region resolves a motivated material-identification gap: it both reconstructs elastic parameters and rejects impossible observations. Global monotonicity and the near-critical long-wave scaling add mathematical structure beyond a routine algebraic substitution. No general unmeasured parameter or experimental robustness is claimed.
